item.title: Nigerians will choose the best product in the marketplace – Obi Media to Governors
item.description: By Henry Umoru, Abuja The media office of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, ahead of the January 16, 2027 election, Peter Obi, has taken a swipe at the state governors, accusing them of pushing to undermine democracy, warning that any election that falls short of being free, fair and transparent will fail. The Peter Obi Media Office, POMR noted that it had become aware of a series of covert attempts by governors to interfere with the democratic process, just as it cautioned that Nigerians would resist any process that did not meet the required standards of free, fair and transparent elections. In a statement signed on Tuesday by the POMR spokesman, Idris Zekeri, he reminded the governors that, despite their alleged fraudulent efforts, they were presenting a poor product and that Nigerians would choose the best option available in the marketplace. Buy Maps Zekeri condemned what it described as the increasing desperation of the governors, who, it said, were turning to electoral manipulation and safeguards for rigging instead of presenting their records of service, performance and achievements. According to the office, Nigerians had had enough and remained determined to reject undeserving leaders who had failed them, adding that the 2027 election would be a defining moment for the country and that Nigerians were resolved to reclaim their country through the power of their votes. The statement also said Peter Obi remained the people’s preferred choice because he embodied the strongest offering in the political arena: a leader defined by competence, capacity, character, compassion and commitment, capable of raising Nigeria from its current condition and restoring its dignity, prosperity and hope. The statement read, “The Peter Obi Media Office has become aware of a series of covert efforts by state governors to undermine the democratic process. It once again cautions that any process that falls short of free, fair, and transparent elections will fail, as Nigerians will resist it. “The Media Office reminds the governors that, regardless of their fraudulent efforts, they are presenting a poor product, and Nigerians will select the best option available in the market. “We therefore condemn the increasing desperation of these governors, who, instead of presenting their records of service, performance, and achievements, are turning to electoral manipulation and safeguards for rigging. “Leadership is a privilege earned through service; it is not a mandate to retain power through deceit, intimidation, or interference with the democratic process. “Nigerians have had enough and remain determined to reject undeserving leaders who have failed them. item.title: US strikes Iran’s Qeshm island – Report
item.description: The United States launched limited strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, US media reported, as Iranian media reported five explosions in quick succession. The reported strikes came as US voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterm elections that threaten President Donald Trump’s grip on power. The strikes, first reported by The Wall Street Journal, hit Qeshm Island, strategically located in the Hormuz waterway, a key flashpoint of the Middle East war that has upended global markets. Unnamed US officials cited by the Journal, CNN, The New York Times and several other outlets, described the attacks as defensive in nature. The Journal said it was just the latest of several undeclared strikes. It also said they had not been publicly announced to avoid the impression Washington intended to resume major combat operations. US Central Command did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment. The US and Israel launched their war with Iran with a massive wave of strikes in late February. The conflict has been stalemated for months. Asked if Israel was involved in the latest reported strikes, an Israeli military spokespeson told AFP, “No”. Israel also held an election last week that saw Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s party come out on top, but still short of a majority. The reported attack came just hours after Trump signaled a deal with Iran “could happen”, as American voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterms dominated by public dissatisfaction with the war and the inflation it has brought. “Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible,” Trump posted on his Truth Social platform. Iranian state news agency IRNA reported five explosions in rapid succession on Qeshm island, and that some residents reported seeing two aircraft flying in its skies. It did not say what was behind the explosions. – Ball in US court – Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, meanwhile, said indirect negotiations were taking place with the US. “Given the sensitivity and gravity of the current situation, consultations and deliberations are very intensive,” Araghchi told state media. On Tuesday, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who has been Tehran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, said that while Iran was ready for war it had given Washington a “rational response”. “The ball is now in America’s court to prevent war.” Oil prices had plunged by more than seven percent on Monday on optimism over a possible end to the eight-month-old conflict. – Reopen the strait – US Vice President JD Vance said both he and Trump were optimistic about securing an agreement. “We’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more,” Vance told reporters on Monday. China also called for a return to diplomacy, while Iran’s security chief discussed the conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin. item.title: Gunmen abduct two visually impaired persons in Plateau, demand N50m ransom
item.description: … as seven escape By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have abducted two visually impaired persons along Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State while they were returning to Jos from Benue State, with their abductors demanding N50 million ransom for their release. The victims were among nine persons travelling in a vehicle to attend a training programme in Benue State, while seven others reportedly escaped when the vehicle came under attack on Monday night. Chairman of the Plateau State chapter of the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities (JONAPWD), Shindol Aaron, who confirmed the incident, said the victims were abducted around 8pm in Riyom LGA. He said, “They were selected to attend a training in Benue State and, from what I gathered, they took off from Jos.” “Along the way, they got information that the event had been postponed to another day, and they were asked to return to their station.” “So, it was on their way back to Jos that they encountered some kidnappers who abducted them.” “They were nine in the vehicle. Seven of them escaped, and two were abducted. So, right now, we have a male and a lady in their custody.” According to him, the abductors had established contact with someone in connection with the release of the victims. He said, “This incident happened yesterday, Monday, in the night, around 8pm around Riyom LGA.” “I have not spoken with the kidnappers, but I was told that they were asking for ransom from somebody who spoke with them.” Aaron said the incident had been reported to security agencies, adding that efforts were ongoing to secure the release of the victims. He said, “We have reported the incident to the security agents, and we are trying to see how they could be released.” “The driver of the vehicle also went to the police station to report.” Another member of the association, Ishaya Ayuba Danjatau, who also confirmed the abduction, said the kidnappers had demanded an N50 million ransom. The member said, “The kidnappers have reached out, and they are demanding N50 million before they can free the two persons in their custody. “Where do they want us to get the money from?” Efforts to obtain the reaction of the Plateau State Police Command spokesman, DSP Alabo Alfred, were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: El Nino Watch: The impacts around the world this week
item.description: With torrential rains in India and Nepal, and drought already devastating South America, this year’s exceptionally strong El Nino is being felt across the globe. It threatens rice and coffee harvests to such an extent that the World Bank expects food prices to rise by 18 percent next year. Here is how El Nino is playing out across AFP’s network. – Cyclone lashes India – Ferocious winds and torrential rain lashed India’s southeastern coast after a cyclone made landfall on Wednesday, killing at least three people and triggering nearly 100,000 evacuations. “Our homes get flooded, and we have to stay in the water,” said Rajeshwari, 65, who gave only one name, after being taken to a government-run shelter near Kakinada, close to the heart of the storm. Cyclones, called hurricanes in the North Atlantic and typhoons in the Pacific, are a regular menace in the Bay of Bengal and northern Indian Ocean. The storm season, however, has been turbocharged by the El Nino weather phenomenon that has contributed to unprecedented warming. Cyclone Arnab then moved on towards Nepal, bringing heavy snowfall to the high Himalayan regions and intense rain through Saturday. – Bolivia declares state of emergency – In Bolivia, drought is affecting 78,000 families in six of the country’s nine departments and has led to the loss of more than 75,000 cattle, according to a government report this week. On Saturday, the Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz declared a state of emergency to free up resources for dealing with the impact of El Nino. “This will be a phenomenon that will have very severe impacts in terms of drought and floods, and we need the cooperation of all institutions,” Paz said. In neighbouring countries such as Peru, El Nino has ramped up temperatures and triggered forest fires that have already claimed the lives of at least 12 people. It has also helped spread the tropical disease dengue fever. In Chile meanwhile it is behind the rainiest October ever recorded in Santiago. – El Nino in numbers – According to the World Bank, food prices are expected to rise by 18 percent between 2025 and 2027, a surge explained both by supply difficulties caused by conflicts and by the anticipated effects of El Nino. Since June, the University of Chicago’s Climate Impact Lab estimates that 484,500 excess heat-related deaths have occurred globally due to the weather phenomenon. The organisation projects about 373,000 additional deaths could occur over the next six months. – Vulnerable crops – Coffee, cocoa, rice… in this “Super” El Nino year, what are the most vulnerable crops? The answer depends on the region, but “from a food-security perspective, the crops of greatest concern are staple foods because they provide the bulk of calories consumed by populations in vulnerable countries,” Maximo Torero, chief economist at the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), told AFP. item.title: Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel dies after collision during match
item.description: Spanish football club CD Tenerife have confirmed the death of their striker, Jesús de Miguel, aged 30, following a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a Spanish second division match. The footballer died on Tuesday, November 3, a day after the incident occurred during Tenerife’s league encounter with Andorra at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López Stadium. The collision happened towards the closing stages of the match, when De Miguel went for a loose ball and Owono rushed out of his goal to clear it. The goalkeeper, who was outside his penalty area, collided heavily with the striker, leaving him unconscious on the pitch. Medical personnel immediately rushed to attend to De Miguel, who was treated for several minutes before being carried off on a stretcher and taken to the University Hospital of Nuestra Señora de Candelaria. The match, which was tied at 2-2, was eventually abandoned in the 108th minute to allow medical personnel to attend to the injured player. Owono was shown a red card following the challenge. Reports from Spanish media indicated that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest following the collision but was resuscitated by medical personnel in the ambulance. Although his condition initially appeared stable, it deteriorated in the early hours of Tuesday. Confirming his death, CD Tenerife announced that the striker passed away at 8am on Tuesday. In a statement expressing its grief, the club said: “Broken with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death of Jesús de Miguel Alameda.” The club added: “There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can ease this feeling of overwhelming sadness. We stand with his devastated family, his loved ones and the entire Tenerife family, who mourn this cruel outcome.” It also conveyed its condolences to his family, friends, teammates and supporters. De Miguel’s family thanked those who had sent messages of support and appealed for privacy during the difficult period. The incident has attracted tributes from football clubs and supporters across Spain, with Barcelona and Real Madrid among those expressing condolences. item.title: Iran Unveils Billboard With Threat Against Trump’s Life
item.description: Iran unveiled a massive billboard and banners pledging to kill US President Donald Trump across Tehran on Tuesday, bringing to a new level the official rhetoric displayed in the capital. “We will kill Trump”, read the billboard towering over the busy Enghelab Square in Tehran, which depicted the US president behind bars with his head bowed. New designs of billboards and displays mocking and vowing revenge against Trump have frequently been set up around Tehran since the war began on February 28 when US-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic Republic’s supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iranians wave flags during a gathering in front of an anti-US billboard depicting US President Donald Trump in Tehran’s Enghelab Square on November 3, 2026. Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP In recent days, renewed diplomatic efforts have been underway to bring Tehran and Washington to the table to prevent a resumption of fighting that has spread across the region and driven prices up globally. Trump, who on Tuesday faces crucial US midterm elections amid voter discontent driven in part by the Iran war, has said that a deal “could happen”. A visitor walks past a painting at an art exhibition against US President Donald Trump, in Tajrish Square in Tehran on November 2, 2026. Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP In the busy Tajrish Square in northern Tehran, an open-air exhibition featured paintings of Trump, including one showing him with his face lying bloodied on the ground as a foot presses down on his head. Another depicted a bomb obscuring his face, in an apparent reference to Belgian surrealist René Magritte’s 1964 painting “The Son of Man”. Visitors walk past a painting at an art exhibition against US President Donald Trump, in Tajrish Square in Tehran on November 2, 2026. Photo by ATTA KENARE / AFP Nearby, a life-sized replica of a jail cell has remained on display, with an actor impersonating Trump spending the day inside. An adjacent screen showed images of the damage caused by US strikes on Iran. Tehran accuses Trump of deliberately targeting civilian sites during the war, including a school and a wedding ceremony, killing dozens of people including women and children. State-sponsored billboards and murals have been a fixture of Iran’s public spaces since the 1979 Islamic revolution, used to honour allies, celebrate military figures and send political messages to adversaries, particularly the United States and Israel. item.title: Kebbi Govt Accuses ADC Of Politicising Private Land Dispute
item.description: The Kebbi State Government has accused the African Democratic Congress (ADC) of politicising a private land dispute in Birnin Kebbi, alleging that the opposition party is spreading misinformation for political gains. The government said investigations by the Ministry of Lands and Housing established that the disputed property, located along Sani Abacha Bypass in Birnin Kebbi, belongs to a private businessman, Alhaji Umar Muhammad Gulumbe. It also accused the opposition party of misrepresenting previous security incidents in the state. Addressing a press conference, the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Yakubu Ahmed, said the controversy followed the demolition of a building on the disputed property on November 26. He explained that the incident attracted public attention after videos circulated on social media, alleging that the state government had deployed earth-moving equipment to demolish a property belonging to the ADC. The Commissioner, however, dismissed the allegations, insisting that the incident was a private land dispute between individuals and had no involvement of the state government. According to him, Umar Muhammad Gulumbe presented documents to establish ownership of the property, including a Certificate of Occupancy reportedly signed by former Governor Senator Adamu Aliero. Ahmed further disclosed that Gulumbe had reported the alleged trespass to the police and submitted a petition to the Ministry of Lands and Housing, which subsequently investigated the matter. He maintained that the state government had no prior involvement in the demolition, stressing that any disagreement over ownership should be resolved through the appropriate legal channels. The Commissioner challenged anyone laying claim to the property to present relevant ownership documents before a competent court rather than resorting to social media allegations. He also called on political actors to exercise restraint in their public statements, warning that the spread of unverified information could heighten political tension and threaten peaceful coexistence in the state. However, the full circumstances surrounding the disputed property, including the competing claims and allegations, remain subject to independent verification and, where necessary, determination by the appropriate authorities. item.title: Gambia Central Bank’s planned sack affects 57 Nigerians, NiDCOM kicks
item.description: By Nkiruka Nnorom The Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NIDCOM) has kicked against a directive by the Central Bank of The Gambia ordering banks to sack non-Gambian employees. Chairman/Chief Executive Officer of NIDCOM, Mrs Abike Dabiri-Erewa, described the September 16 directive as deeply worrisome, saying it threatens the jobs of 57 Nigerian professionals. Dabiri-Erewa, in a statement by NIDCOM spokesman Abdur-Rahman Balogun, said the Central Bank of The Gambia (CBG) had given banks till December 31, 2026, to replace all non-Gambian staff with Gambians. NIDCOM said the affected Nigerians work with four Nigerian-owned banks and hold valid residency and work permits. The Commission noted that the four banks are major players in the Gambian economy, controlling 37.2 per cent of total deposits valued at GMD35.3 billion, 32.6 per cent of loans amounting to GMD7.67 billion and 37 per cent of industry assets worth GMD44.78 billion. The banks, it added, also account for 34.5 per cent of investments in Central Bank bonds and provided 90 per cent of funding for the National Water and Electricity Company, NAWEC. While acknowledging The Gambia’s right to promote local employment, Dabiri-Erewa said such policy must respect existing contracts, valid work permits and ECOWAS protocols on free movement. She said, “It is contradictory to encourage African investment and regional cooperation while displacing qualified African professionals.” NIDCOM urged the apex bank to reverse the blanket directive and engage the Nigerian High Commission in Banjul and other stakeholders for an amicable resolution. It also called on Gambian authorities to uphold the spirit of ECOWAS integration and the long-standing cordial relations between Nigeria and The Gambia. item.title: Kano APC dismisses Kwankwaso’s allegation over missing NDC guber candidate’s name
item.description: The APC in Kano has dismissed Sen. Rabiu Kwankwaso’s claim that it and Gov. Abba Yusuf omitted NDC candidate’s name from INEC list. The candidate in question is Aminu Abdussalam-Gwarzo of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). This is contained in a statement issued by the Chairman, All Progressives Congress (APC), Kano State, Alhaji Umar Haruna-Doguwa, made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Tuesday in Kano. “The party described the allegation as false, baseless and an attempt by Kwankwaso to blackmail the APC and its governorship candidate. “The APC maintained that the case originated from the internal crisis within the NDC. “Neither the party nor Gov. Yusuf has any involvement whatsoever in the legal proceedings surrounding the NDC candidate. “It was instituted by party members against the NDC itself, and not by the APC, its governorship candidate or the Kano State Government,” he said. The chairman stressed that attempts to associate the APC and its candidate with the matter were misleading and intended to shift attention from the internal challenges confronting the NDC. Haruna-Doguwa said the party distanced itself from the legal proceedings, insisting that neither the APC nor its governorship candidate sponsored, influenced or facilitated the court action against Abdussalam-Gwarzo. “The judiciary is an independent arm of government and neither the APC nor its governorship candidate has the authority to dictate its proceedings or decisions,” he said. He challenged Sen. Kwankwaso to provide credible and verifiable evidence linking the APC or Gov. Yusuf to the case, rather than making allegations capable of misleading the public and creating unnecessary political tension. “The APC described the allegation as an unfortunate attempt at political blackmail, particularly coming from Sen. Kwankwaso, who is the Vice-Presidential candidate of the NDC,” he said. Haruna-Doguwa added that every eligible candidate has the constitutional right to participate in the 2027 general elections in accordance with the law. He reaffirmed the APC’s commitment to democratic principles and welcomed the participation of opposition parties in the electoral process, stressing that it has no reason to plot against any political party or candidate. The chairman called on the public to disregard attempts to associate the APC and its governorship candidate with the NDC’s internal legal battle. Haruna-Doguwa reiterated that neither the party nor its candidate had any hand, directly or indirectly, in the proceedings or any decision concerning the party’s candidate. (NAN) The post Kano APC dismisses Kwankwaso’s allegation over missing NDC guber candidate’s name appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Okada rider stabs 25-year-old boxer to death in Ibadan
item.description: By Adeola Badru IBADAN — A 25-year-old amateur boxer, identified simply as Kehinde and popularly known as KBlaq, has been stabbed to death by a commercial motorcyclist following a dispute over transport fare at Olodo Garage, Lagelu Local Government Area of Oyo State. The incident reportedly occurred after a disagreement between the deceased and the motorcyclist over payment of an agreed fare, triggering tension in the area and disrupting commercial activities. An eyewitness said the disagreement began after Kehinde allegedly failed to honour an agreement reached with the rider over the fare, leading to a heated argument that escalated into a physical confrontation. It was gathered that during the altercation, the motorcyclist allegedly brought out a sharp object and stabbed the boxer. Kehinde reportedly sustained fatal injuries and died following the attack. The killing has heightened tension around Olodo Garage, with commercial motorcyclists reportedly withdrawing their services amid fears of possible reprisal attacks. The withdrawal has disrupted transportation in the area, forcing commuters to trek long distances to their destinations, while traders and other residents have also been affected by the disruption to daily activities. Confirming the incident in a telephone conversation with our correspondent, the Oyo State Police Public Relations Officer, Ayanlade Olayinka, said the matter was under investigation. item.title: North Korea test fires strategic cruise missiles
item.description: North Korea test-fired strategic cruise missiles, state media reported Tuesday, in the latest display of its weapons capabilities as tensions persist on the Korean peninsula. The Monday launch came a day after North Korea tested cluster bomb warheads, as tensions with Seoul have risen after a landmine blast along their heavily fortified border wounded three South Korean soldiers. “The middle-sized dispersal warhead tipped on the cruise missile is capable of turning into ashes a target area of 5 to 6 hectares with its highest-density power,” the official Korean Central News Agency reported Tuesday. The test “perfected the capability to deliver a vertical strike against the target by improving the terminal maneuverability of the cruise missile,” KCNA said, “taking into consideration the natural and geographical characteristics of the targeted area.” A North Korean official was quoted as saying the test was conducted “because our armed forces should defend the security of the country and deter all sorts of threats.” “Various combat functions of such strongest weapon system will help defend the DPRK from potential threats from outside and renew the military capabilities of the state,” the general director of the Missile Administration said, using the acronym for North Korea’s official name. The nuclear-armed North recently trialled a range of weaponry including attack drones, a new precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile. South Korea’s military did not announce the cruise missile launch, as it had also not done with Sunday’s test. Unlike ballistic missile launches, North Korean cruise missile tests are not prohibited by UN Security Council sanctions. Asked Monday about Sunday’s reported test, Joint Chiefs of Staff spokesperson Jang Do-young said South Korea and the United States were “closely coordinating and conducting a highly detailed analysis of its characteristics and specifications”. “Our military does not announce all projectiles launched by North Korea,” said Jang. “Whether to make an announcement is determined through a comprehensive military assessment, taking into account the protection of surveillance and reconnaissance assets and capabilities, operational security and other factors,” he added. item.title: Soludo confirms Peter Obi’s wife as child’s godmother
item.description: Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has confirmed that the wife of former governor Peter Obi is the godmother of one of his children, months after a public disagreement over the relationship between their families. Soludo also disclosed that his wife, Nonye, is the confirmation godmother of Obi’s daughter, clarifying the family relationship that became a subject of public discussion in September. The governor made the disclosure in an interview with BBC News Igbo on Monday, describing Obi as a close friend and insisting that their families remained on good terms despite their political differences. “Peter Obi and I are good friends. Our two families are on good terms. His wife was the godmother of my child at baptism, and my wife was the godmother of his child at confirmation,” he said. Soludo explained that their differences were political, particularly over their preferences for who should govern Anambra State. He said he did not hold Obi’s political position against him, despite their disagreement over the state’s leadership. “I have a different vision of who should be governor of Anambra State. I am contesting, and he supported whoever he felt should be governor. I prevailed by the grace of God, and I don’t hold it against him,” the governor said. item.title: Utomi faults APC over alleged extravagance amid hardship
item.description: Political economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration over what he described as extravagant lifestyles among public officials amid economic hardship in the country. Utomi said it was contradictory for government officials to describe Nigeria as poor while allegedly displaying luxury vehicles, including Maybachs, G-Wagons and Rolls-Royces, and travelling in private jets. He made the remarks in a post on his X account on Tuesday, arguing that the lifestyles of public office holders should reflect the economic realities confronting ordinary Nigerians. “You cannot stand before the world and declare that Nigeria is poor, then turn around and parade your ministers in million-dollar Maybachs, G-Wagons and Rolls-Royces, while public officials fly around in private jets. Your optics contradict your narrative, your lifestyle contradicts your statistics,” he said. The former presidential candidate said if Nigeria was indeed poor, government spending and the management of public resources should reflect the country’s economic circumstances. He argued that members of the executive and legislature should demonstrate fiscal restraint, particularly when citizens were being asked to endure economic difficulties. According to him, public office should not be treated as a licence for extravagance, adding that government officials had a responsibility to show restraint in the use of public resources. “The APC needs to understand that public office is not a licence for extravagance. If citizens must endure economic hardship, those entrusted with their taxes must also demonstrate restraint,” Utomi said. He added that displaying luxury lifestyles while asking Nigerians to endure economic hardship could deepen public resentment and reinforce perceptions that government officials were insensitive to the plight of ordinary citizens. item.title: Police rescue 11 kidnapped victims, arrest 19 suspects
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has rescued 11 kidnapped victims, arrested 19 suspects and recovered 91 rustled livestock, including 48 cows and 43 sheep, in security operations conducted across several states in the last 48 hours. The operations also led to the recovery of firearms, stolen valuables and motorcycles, while several attempted bandit attacks were foiled. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, disclosed the operational breakthroughs in a statement on Tuesday, saying the operations were part of sustained efforts to combat kidnapping, terrorism, armed robbery, cultism, cattle rustling and other criminal activities. He said investigations and follow-up operations were ongoing to apprehend fleeing suspects, rescue more victims and recover stolen property. In Zamfara State, police tactical operatives, working with local vigilantes, rescued five elderly women abducted by armed bandits while harvesting beans in Dansadau, Maru Local Government Area. The victims were freed following a gun battle that forced the abductors to flee. However, a 35-year-old farmer was killed during the attack. In Niger State, a joint security team comprising police, military personnel, Department of State Services operatives, special hunters and vigilantes rescued six farmers abducted at Mahangi village, near Pandogari in Rafi Local Government Area. The victims were subsequently taken to a police division for documentation and reunion with their families. In Kebbi State, joint security forces repelled an attack by suspected Lakurawa terrorists on Ribah town in Danko Wasagu Local Government Area on October 30, after the attackers attempted to block Rambo Junction. The operation followed an earlier attack on Dan-Indo village in Fakai Local Government Area, where nine people were killed, while two vehicles and several motorcycles were set ablaze. The police said security operatives had been deployed to maintain order and sustain operations against the suspected terrorists. Also in Zamfara, police and soldiers have launched a coordinated search-and-rescue operation following the abduction of nine persons at Upa, near Kurya Madaro in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area. Bush-combing operations are ongoing in surrounding forests to secure their release and apprehend the perpetrators. In Kano State, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad arrested five suspects accused of harbouring criminals in connection with the abduction of the APC Chairman of Rogo Local Government Area, Alhaji Abdu Fanka. Although the principal suspects reportedly escaped, the police recovered 48 cows, 43 sheep and two Bajaj Boxer motorcycles from the location. In Katsina State, tactical teams foiled an attempted bandit attack on Karofi village in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area after responding to a distress call. item.title: 2027: Atiku’s presidency won’t determine Senate President, Reps Speaker — Melaye
item.description: The Deputy Director-General of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Dino Melaye, has said a government led by Atiku Abubakar will not determine who becomes Senate President or Speaker of the House of Representatives. Melaye said the ADC would allow lawmakers to elect their leaders independently, insisting that the party was committed to democratic principles and an independent National Assembly. He stated this while answering questions on the oversight mechanisms the ADC would introduce to track government payments, fund releases and beneficiaries during an appearance on Arise Television’s Prime Time on Monday. “To start with, an Atiku presidency will not determine who is going to be the Senate president, the president of the Senate, or the Speaker of the House of Representatives,” he said. “Atiku is a Democrat. ADC is a very democratic political party. So we are going to allow the people to elect their leaders.” Melaye argued that allowing lawmakers to choose their leaders would promote legislative independence and strengthen the National Assembly’s oversight of the executive arm of government. “And I told you that wherever you have the members electing their leaders, there is some modicum of independence,” he said. “So to start with, the ADC will make sure that the National Assembly is truly independent, and if the National Assembly is truly independent, that will drive their oversight functions over the Executive.” On the mechanisms for scrutinising government spending, the ADC campaign official said relevant National Assembly committees would be empowered to question government officials and monitor expenditure. He specifically identified the Committees on Establishment, Finance, and Budget and Planning as possible channels for investigating government spending and ensuring accountability. “The Committee on Establishment is responsible for questioning this type of spenders because they have direct oversight function over the State House. The committee on finance is there. item.title: Atiku faults Cross River security over alleged estate robberies
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has criticised the security arrangements around Cross River State Governor’s private residence in Calabar, following reports of alleged robberies in neighbouring homes. Atiku said residents of the estate where Governor Bassey Otu’s private residence is located had complained of repeated burglaries despite the presence of armed policemen and two roadblocks securing the governor’s property. According to him, one resident reportedly lost an air conditioner and a freezer to burglars, while another disclosed that two houses on a nearby street were attacked last week. The former Vice President disclosed this in a post on his X account on Tuesday, questioning the disparity between the security provided for the governor and the protection available to residents living in the same neighbourhood. He said the governor had been operating from his private residence for nearly three years while the Government House was undergoing renovation, yet residents living nearby remained exposed to security threats. “This is security, APC style: two roadblocks for the governor, and none for the people next door,” Atiku said. He questioned the capacity of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to address insecurity across the state, asking what it could offer communities outside the state capital if residents living beside the governor could not sleep without fear. Atiku also outlined his proposed security reforms, pledging to transform the Nigeria Police Force from what he described as a regime-protecting force into a citizen-focused public service. He said his administration would expand police personnel towards the international benchmark of one officer to every 450 citizens to improve security coverage across communities. The ADC presidential candidate also promised to establish community-based security and intelligence networks to enable neighbourhoods to identify and report threats before criminal activities occur. “Security that stops at the governor’s gate is not security; it is a fence,” he added. item.title: WARRI DELINEATION: Lawyer seeks probe, warns against political manipulation, violence
item.description: Lawyer and politician, Chief Robinson Ariyo, has urged President Bola Tinubu to investigate the Warri delineation exercise, saying there are allegations of financial inducement to favour some areas over others. Ariyo also called on the President to direct the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice to provide an independent written legal opinion on the legality of the exercise. In a statement, he urged the President to direct relevant agencies to preserve all documents and records relating to the exercise and investigate allegations of financial misconduct, security compromises and electoral irregularities. He further called for an independent forensic audit of private surveillance contracts relating to Nigeria’s oil and gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta, particularly those whose financial transactions, beneficiaries or performance records might be connected to the allegations surrounding the Warri delineation controversy. Ariyo also urged the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, ICPC, and Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit, NFIU, to investigate credible allegations of suspicious dollar transactions, unexplained financial inflows and possible financial inducement of political actors, public officers, electoral personnel and security operatives in connection with the controversy. The statement reads: “That the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice be requested to provide an independent, written legal opinion on the legality of the ongoing Warri delineation exercise, identifying the applicable constitutional provisions, statutory powers, judicial orders and procedural requirements governing the exercise. The opinion should specifically distinguish between the delineation of electoral wards, State Constituencies and Federal Constituencies. “That INEC be formally requested, in the exercise of its constitutional independence, to publish the complete delineation report, supporting maps, methodology, relevant population and geographical data, stakeholder submissions and reasons for accepting or rejecting material objections. That the Commission be urged to undertake a transparent review of any substantiated procedural or factual irregularities and refrain from implementing any aspect found to be unlawful, subject always to applicable judicial orders and statutory requirements. “That all relevant documents, correspondence, meeting records, maps, electronic records, financial documents and administrative communications relating to the exercise be preserved against destruction, alteration or concealment. “That the appropriate federal authorities undertake an independent forensic audit of private surveillance contracts relating to Nigeria’s oil and gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta, particularly contracts whose financial transactions, beneficiaries or performance records may be relevant to the allegations raised herein. item.title: Abia picked for regional stroke, neurovascular centre
item.description: . As Otti govt secures int’l recognition for health reforms By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State has emerged as the preferred location for a proposed stroke and neurovascular centre to serve Nigeria and West Africa, following its participation in the 2026 Sweden-Africa Neurosurgery Symposium in Gothenburg, Sweden. The state Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this while briefing newsmen on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Alex Otti at Government House, Umuahia. Kanu said the selection was in recognition of Abia’s strides in healthcare delivery and the availability of qualified medical specialists, describing it as another milestone in the state’s ongoing health sector reforms. He said the proposed centre would address the rising incidence of stroke across Africa, particularly Nigeria, by providing specialised facilities for comprehensive treatment and management of neurovascular conditions. According to him, the state government had approved the participation of the Ministry of Health in the international symposium to explore strategic partnerships and opportunities for specialised healthcare development. The Commissioner said Abia’s health sector reforms were also showcased at the symposium, adding that the Ministry of Health had recently been recognised as a national self-care champion. He said the recognition underscored the state’s growing capacity to promote preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyles among residents. On public health preparedness, Kanu disclosed that the government had established a multi-sectoral frontline technical working group to strengthen emergency response mechanisms. He said the group had developed an Ebola preparedness and response plan, while the government had expanded the deployment of modern medical technology in specialised healthcare. Kanu further disclosed that the Infectious Disease Hospital in Aba had been completed, alongside an infectious disease facility and specialist hospital in Umuahia, as part of efforts to strengthen the state’s capacity to tackle Ebola and other infectious diseases. He, however, said no cases of Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera or avian influenza were recorded in Abia. The Commissioner also announced progress in the agricultural intervention programme being implemented across the state’s 17 local government areas in partnership with the councils. He said the initiative was designed to attract investments, boost food production, develop viable agricultural enterprises and create employment through strengthened agricultural value chains. The Commissioner disclosed that Arochukwu LGA had a plantation plantation of over 86,000 trees, describing it as highly commendable. On housing, Kanu said the government’s residential development at Pocket Layout had attracted overwhelming interest, with applications exceeding available units. item.title: NIMC arrests illegal NIN operators, seizes enrolment equipment
item.description: By Emmanuel Elebeke The National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) has intensified its crackdown on illegal National Identification Number (NIN) enrolment, unauthorised data modification and extortion, following an enforcement operation that led to several arrests in Gwagwalada and other locations. The Commission disclosed this in a statement, saying its Inspectorate Compliance and Enforcement Unit (ICEU) carried out the operation and seized equipment allegedly used for illegal enrolment activities. It said the exercise was part of efforts to curb unauthorised enrolment and unethical practices while protecting the integrity, security and credibility of Nigeria’s National Identity Management System. NIMC noted that many of the challenges encountered by NIN holders resulted from attempts to bypass official enrolment procedures. It stressed that NIN enrolment could only be conducted at its approved centres, while requests for modification of personal data could be processed through its self-service modification platform. The Commission also advised NIN holders to download the NINAuth application from the iOS App Store or Google Play Store to access security features, print their NIN slips and enjoy other related services. The Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of NIMC, Engr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote, reiterated the Commission’s zero tolerance for extortion and unethical practices. She said the Commission remained committed to providing seamless and hitch-free NIN enrolment services for Nigerians and legal residents. NIMC urged applicants and existing NIN holders to use only its approved channels for enrolment and other related services. It advised members of the public to visit www.nimc.gov.ng or follow its verified social media platforms for accurate information. item.title: Five officers’ final duty in Zamfara
item.description: From Abdullahi Abdulrahaman Chakwa (Gusau), Salim Umar Ibrahim (Kano) & Dalhatu Liman (Abuja) Five police officers have been killed and several others injured in an ambush by bandits at Gidan Kano on the Gusau-Sokoto highway in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. The officers were travelling in an 18-seater bus belonging to the Zamfara State Transport Authority when they were attacked on Monday morning. The security personnel were reportedly on their way to provide security during the All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial rerun primary in Zamfara North Senatorial District when the incident occurred. A witness, who spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity, said the bandits lay in ambush for the security operatives as they travelled along the highway. He said about five officers were feared killed, while several others sustained varying degrees of injury. “The bandits lay in ambush for the security personnel travelling in the Zamfara State Transport Authority bus. Five of them were killed, while many others were injured. The bullets penetrated the bus from different angles,” he said. However, another resident, who also spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity, claimed that eight security personnel were killed, while several others were abducted by the gunmen. He said residents helped to evacuate the bodies of the deceased officers but could not account for some of the other personnel. “Eight security personnel were killed, and we helped to load their corpses into two different vehicles. We suspect that the remaining officers were abducted because they could not be found,” he added. In a related development, bandits ambushed workers of a telecommunications company at Tungan Tama village, along the same Gusau-Sokoto highway, a few kilometres from the scene of the attack at Gidan Kano. One person was reportedly killed, while several others sustained injuries in the attack on the telecommunications workers. “The bandits attacked them at Tungan Tama village, but they managed to reach Tashar Mayanchi, where we discovered that one person had been killed,” a resident said. Daily Trust gathered that bandits had carried out several attacks on communities along the highway, targeting travellers, residents and workers. The repeated attacks, involving road blockades, ambushes and kidnappings, have raised concerns about the safety of the strategic highway linking Zamfara State with Sokoto and other parts of the North-West. Commuters using the route continue to face the risk of being caught in attacks, while residents and motorists have expressed fears over the growing insecurity along the corridor. Police confirm attack on officers The spokesperson of the Zone 10 Police Command headquarters in Sokoto, ASP Abdallah Faruk Ambursa, confirmed the attack.
